Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

shinyOAuthDB 0.0.0.9000

  • Add oauth_db_supabase_api() for Supabase tables, views and functions using project publishable keys and each visitor’s access token. Add oauth_db_supabase_client() for the project’s OAuth server, with a setup guide covering native sign-in, third-party providers and row-level security.

  • Generalize oauth_db_oracle() to database-trusted OAuth JWTs, including configured OCI IAM OAuth and Keycloak direct-logon integrations. Add authorization_model = "end_user" to verify Oracle Deep Data Security token context and reopen sessions when renewed tokens carry new claims. Oracle operation scopes are now checked literally for every provider.

  • Add oauth_db_oracle_ords_api() for protected ORDS collections and JSON resources with per-visitor OAuth tokens. Preserve native pages, enforce session isolation and retry only safe reads. Add generic OIDC and provider-specific setup guides.

  • Install the checkout’s source archive in Docker demo browser checks and verify its hash in the running app container before testing sign-in.

  • Decode Turso’s null-valued floating-point results as NaN, preserving SQL NULL values and rejecting malformed float cells in ordinary and raw results.

  • Allow Azure PostgreSQL to share a Microsoft sign-in client with other services by requesting its explicit delegated scope in mixed-service clients.

  • Add oauth_db_oracle() for Oracle Database configured for Microsoft Entra authentication. Connections use Oracle ODBC, verified TCPS and each visitor’s access token. Temporary token files are removed after connection opening; the helper requires Oracle to confirm token authentication. Includes a setup guide for self-hosted and hosted databases.

  • Document ODBC as the Fabric backend for dbplyr’s SQL Server translations, and explain ADBC driver setup, result lifetime and numeric conversion.

  • Apply ODBC connection-string validation only to Fabric’s ODBC backend, allowing literal ADBC driver paths. Reject URI overrides for either backend.

  • Reopen Fabric ADBC connections with a current token on access after token renewal, without replaying completed reactive queries. ODBC connections continue to reuse valid database sessions across ordinary token renewal.

  • Close ADBC connections and their outstanding DBI or Arrow results when the authorization changes, permissions are lost, or the Shiny session ends.

  • Return CrateDB’s internal byte columns as numbers, including nulls and empty results, and reject values outside the signed byte range in scalar and array responses.

  • Decode libSQL REAL values as doubles regardless of JSON number notation, while retaining exact integer cells and large affected-row counts.

  • Retain the selected Microsoft resource’s default consent scopes when using token_targets = list(). Multiple resources need named targets or explicit scopes instead of silently requesting only sign-in permissions.

  • Refuse to restart an active services-mode demo at the same database and path, preventing competing handles from stopping its containers or restoring its OAuth options prematurely.

  • Parse API responses and HTTP error diagnostics as literal JSON so response bodies cannot trigger local-file reads or additional HTTP requests.

  • Refresh the Docker demo runtime to include the current transport protections, corrected local app ports, strict date decoding and exact row-count checks.

  • Check CrateDB row-count limits before numeric conversion so counts above 2^53 cannot round into the supported range.

  • Reject malformed BigQuery and ClickHouse dates, including invalid calendar dates and trailing text, while preserving nulls and typed empty results.

  • Use the published relay port in generated local PostgreSQL and StarRocks apps, independent of argument line breaks in the Docker app templates.

  • Convert CrateDB query results to data frames once, while retaining cell validation for raw results and execution counts.

  • Reject malformed BigQuery Boolean, floating-point and timestamp results, including nested values, instead of silently introducing missing data. Preserve SQL NULLs and valid floating-point NaN and infinity values.

  • Return the complete CrateDB SQL endpoint from services-mode demos so demo$url can be passed directly to oauth_db_cratedb_api().

  • Prevent libcurl from replaying PostgREST, OpenSearch, ClickHouse and CrateDB writes after a reused connection drops its response. Apply the existing libSQL protection through the shared HTTP transport.

  • Reject Snowflake ODBC protocol overrides before acquiring a token or opening a native connection, preserving the driver’s HTTPS default.

  • Require token-based password authentication over verified TLS for Azure PostgreSQL. Disable GSS encryption and reject native authentication/TLS overrides. This helper now requires RPostgres linked to libpq 16 or later.

  • Reject incomplete BigQuery dataset listings when the API reports unreachable locations, including on later result pages.

  • Restore services-mode OAuth options and revoke its PostgREST HTTP exception when stopping through oauth_db_demo(action = "stop"). Retained handles recognize the shutdown, and failed Docker cleanup remains retryable.

  • Launch the documented apps with runApp(..., launch.browser = FALSE) and explain that OAuth sign-in needs a regular browser. Keep the README’s follow-up links in a short Learn more section.

  • Add oauth_db_demo(action = "services") to start Docker infrastructure and return settings for an app running in the current R session. The README example now starts PostgreSQL and PostgREST itself, works without a native database driver, and stops its services when Shiny stops.

  • Keep the README app focused on sign-in and a PostgreSQL query. Ship that minimal example in the package with Docker run instructions. Runnable demos keep their styled UI.

  • Use alice / alice and bob / bob for demo sign-in, with explicit username/password tables. Remove “Your” from cloud demo titles and keep sign-in guidance in sync with completed queries and warehouse selection.

  • Give all local and cloud demos a responsive bslib layout, with sign-in controls, visible example queries/requests and platform-specific connection details. Local R and cloud apps require bslib 0.9.0 or later.

  • Clarify each local demo’s purpose, demo accounts and expected data access. Show editing and restart commands in the console, and let users retry a failed write check without losing the Shiny session.

  • Keep cloud drafts in a persistent directory per platform. Back to setup now offers a settings menu without discarding the client registration. Cloud apps explain their identity query and guide sign-in and query errors.

  • Add a ClickHouse Cloud demo for a qualifying JWT service with Entra role mapping, an early readiness check and HTTPS SQL requests.

  • Add a Redshift cloud demo using Entra JWTs and IAM Identity Center, with a readiness check and explicit resource/scope guidance.

  • Add an Azure PostgreSQL cloud demo with Entra user/group-role mapping, a trusted CA bundle and RPostgres connections.

  • Add an Azure SQL cloud demo with Entra database-principal and networking guidance, and separate local Shiny and database ports.

  • Add a Snowflake cloud demo with custom integration instructions, matching OAuth/SQL roles and explicit warehouse selection.

  • Add a BigQuery cloud demo with Web OAuth registration guidance, query project/location settings and a maximum bytes billed limit.

  • Add a guided Fabric cloud demo with Entra registration help, editable SQL app files and an explicit query button. Cloud drafts are now isolated by platform and use platform-specific secret environment variables.

  • Add oauth_db_cloud_demo("databricks"), a cli console guide that prepares an editable local Shiny app, supports public and confidential OAuth app registrations, and explains why Free Edition lacks its registration path.

  • Add $warehouses() to the Databricks API client, with paginated discovery using the signed-in visitor’s authorization.

  • Add app = "local" to oauth_db_demo(): keep the database and sign-in services in Docker and run an editable Shiny app with your local R library. The default continues to run the app in Docker.

  • Extend oauth_db_demo() with DuckDB Quack, libSQL, CrateDB and OpenSearch. Each includes browser sign-in, server-validated tokens and sample data; the apps also demonstrate database rejection of writes.

  • Add oauth_db_demo() to launch packaged PostgreSQL, PostgREST, Trino and StarRocks Docker demos with sign-in and sample data, without a checkout.

  • Keep one PostgreSQL example in the README and add a pkgdown website with database guides, OAuth registration instructions and local demo help.

  • Add oauth_db_libsql_api() for SQL queries and statements against libSQL and compatible Turso HTTPS endpoints. Supports bound parameters, exact 64-bit integers, blobs and mixed SQLite types. Each operation uses a fresh stream and connection; SQL is never retried after a lost response or 401. Includes a real libSQL/JWT/TLS fixture and provider compatibility guidance.

  • Add oauth_db_cratedb_api() for CrateDB’s JWT-authenticated HTTPS SQL interface, positional parameters and exact BIGINT/NUMERIC results. Tokens are renewed before requests, and SQL submissions are never replayed.

  • Add oauth_db_opensearch_api() for Query DSL, aggregations, SQL plugin queries and native JSON requests with a visitor’s current bearer token. Preserves nested results and metadata, rejects incomplete searches, and includes a native OpenSearch Security JWT/TLS permission fixture.

  • Add oauth_db_duckdb() for DBI and dbplyr queries against OAuth-enabled DuckDB Quack servers. Connections use TLS by default and are replaced when access tokens rotate; sign-out and session end shut down their private in-memory DuckDB instances.

  • Add oauth_db_clickhouse_api() for JWT-authenticated HTTPS queries and statements. Supports native typed parameters, exact integers and decimals, metadata, and list columns. SQL submissions are never replayed automatically.

  • Add oauth_db_starrocks() for DBI queries through StarRocks JWT authentication and MySQL Connector/ODBC. Temporary token files are removed after connection opening; account and username changes replace connections.

  • Add oauth_db_postgrest_api() for tables, views, functions, and native PostgREST requests with each visitor’s current token. Reads support filters, schema selection, pagination, and a single 401 refresh retry. Writes and POST function calls are not replayed automatically.

  • Require shinyOAuth 0.7.0 and httr2 1.2.0.

  • Add oauth_db_postgres() for self-hosted PostgreSQL 18 with native OAuth on Linux/libpq 18, a Docker/Keycloak playground, and a separate browser integration workflow that exercises database grants and row policies.

  • Add connection helpers for Azure SQL, Fabric SQL, Databricks SQL, Snowflake, Redshift, Trino, and Azure PostgreSQL. Query with DBI or dbplyr; helpers reuse connections and call the driver’s cleanup method when the authorization or session ends. Retained Databricks handles can keep their copied tokens; call the helper before each operation.

  • Add oauth_db_bigquery_client() for Google sign-in and oauth_db_bigquery_api() for GoogleSQL queries. The query client returns data frames and supports named parameters.

  • Add oauth_db_fabric_api() and oauth_db_databricks_api() to call fabricQueryR and brickster functions with the user’s credentials. Fabric resource objects can use the same sign-in for later methods.

  • Add Microsoft, Databricks, and Snowflake sign-in presets. Existing shinyOAuth clients can also be used.

  • Replace the earlier source and operation API with Shiny reactive code and database functions. See the migration notes.

  • Add a guide for each source, with sign-in setup and a complete app.
